newsitem.title: GERMANY: U-Freight's Internet site has 1,000 daily hits.
newsitem.headline: U-Freight's Internet site has 1,000 daily hits.

text.p: International freight forwarder U-Freight said clients were tracking and tracing air cargo shipments up to 1,000 times a day through its Internet site.
N.S. Cheong, U-Freight owner and director, said: "We now have to up 1,000 hits a day after one and a half years with the Internet page."
This usage was relatively low but tracking and tracing was only used by clients when problems occurred, he pointed out.
Cheong said the U-Freight Internet site amounted to "a virtual warehouse somewhere in cyberspace" linked into all major airfreight systems such as Traxon and SITA.
Gene Boyer, U-Freight managing director Americas & Europe, claimed the company's Internet tracking and tracing system was comparable in standard to those of integrators such as Fedex or UPS.
Customers could even search for items under their own company parts numbers and not an airway bill or U-Freight number, he stressed.
Use of the Internet avoided having to link different company systems and allowed open access to all customers, Boyer noted.
But some airlines were slow to key in shipment data meaning there was sometimes an information delay while goods were being flown airport to airport, he criticised.
"We have been pushing the airlines to update their systems more. Sometimes they first key in the information at the end of the day when the freight has already arrived," he said.
But Cheong added: "Traxon is accurate in its data. We are pretty happy with the airlines' performance in updating." - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017
